summary: <cite index="1-4">Wall Street closed higher on Friday as weak jobs data for July raised hope that the Federal Reserve may hold interest rates steady for longer.</cite> <cite index="8-4">Stocks surged last Friday on lowered rate hike expectations after a surprise negative July payroll reading raised fears about the jobs market.</cite> However, <cite index="5-11,5-12,5-13">the S&P 500 was relatively unchanged on Monday amid growing doubts that the U.S. and Iran will come to a lasting resolution to the conflict in the near term. The broad index traded down 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.4%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 136 points, or 0.3%.</cite> <cite index="5-3">Oil rose Monday, as traders continue to assess mixed signals from the U.S. and Iran amid worries that a deal between both countries to open the Strait of Hormuz may not be anytime soon.</cite> <cite index="5-14">Intel was a key laggard of the session, falling 3% after the company said it's going to be offering $15 billion in common stock.</cite> Meanwhile, <cite index="44-11,44-12,44-13">while the price of ethereum continues to hold within a narrow price range, the price of bitcoin has hit high marks above $65,000 for the past four days. Bitcoin and ethereum prices moved upward following a much more negative jobs report on Friday than many economists had predicted. Analysts reduced expectations for a September Fed rate increase following the July employment report, but with two key inflation reports expected this week, we'll see if the rate-change scales tip back in the other direction.</cite>

signals.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions drive oil above $85, pressure equities
signals.desc: Iran insists the U.S. must meet several demands before reopening the Strait of Hormuz, pushing WTI oil prices up 2% and pressuring stock indexes amid renewed inflation concerns.

signals.title: Intel announces $15B stock offering, shares drop 4%
signals.desc: Intel's massive dilutive equity raise sent shares tumbling 4% and dragged semiconductor and tech names lower, contributing to Nasdaq underperformance.

signals.title: Weak July jobs data reduces Fed rate hike expectations
signals.desc: A surprise negative July payroll reading cooled expectations for additional Fed rate hikes, boosting risk assets including stocks and crypto on Friday.

signals.title: Bitcoin holds above $65,000 for fourth consecutive day
signals.desc: Bitcoin sustained gains above $65,000 on softer Fed rate hike expectations, while crypto ETFs saw $1.1 billion in inflows last week despite low trading volume.

signals.title: CPI and PPI inflation data loom mid-week
signals.desc: Key inflation reports due Tuesday and Wednesday could reshape rate expectations and determine whether Friday's dovish pivot holds or reverses, creating volatility.

verdict: Markets drift near all-time highs but face headwinds from Strait of Hormuz tensions and upcoming CPI data that could reshape rate expectations and test recent dovish pivot.
